notes: E4 measures the SHIPPED PATH: every task is executed by shelling out to
`node v0/src/cli/index.mjs run <task>` exactly as a developer would, with no special
flags and the default posture. This is deliberately different from eval/real/, which
drives a harness-agnostic runner interface over five tiny npm libraries. See the
conflict note in run-e4.mjs.
SCHEMA 2 — SUBTREE WORKSPACES (revised after the E4 pilot). The first manifest pointed
each task at a WHOLE repo copy. The pilot exposed that every one of the six repos is
itself an agent framework: the harness (correctly, per W7) loaded the workspace's own
AGENTS.md plus 137 skills into the system prompt (~44KB for ruflo), which this local
model cannot turn around inside the shipped 60s model request timeout — so every whole-
repo task failed at the provider layer before the model could produce output.
This revision therefore points each task at a REAL, dependency-free SUBTREE of its repo
(the ruflo-adr/scripts pattern proven by the E3 control run at 15.4s): a few kilobytes
of third-party source with no AGENTS.md, no CLAUDE.md, and no skills directory in the
copied workspace, so the prompt is small and the shipped timeout is not the test. The
tree under research/repos/ is never written to; each run copies only the subtree.
The untunable 60s request timeout itself is logged as a product finding, not silently
patched mid-measurement.
SEEDED BUGS. A mini_bugfix task applies the exact one-line `seed` replacement below to
the TEMP COPY before the run starts. Each seed was chosen to be a plausible single-line
regression in a pure function, and each `verify` command asserts the ORIGINAL correct
behaviour — so it fails before the run and passes only if the model actually restored it.
Every `verify` command runs with node and stdlib only: the copied subtree is dependency-
free and the sandbox is not permitted to reach the network.

tasks.task: In lib/parse-adrs.mjs the function normalizeAdrId is wrong: normalizeAdrId('7') returns 'ADR-07' but it must return 'ADR-007' (IDs shorter than 4 digits are zero-padded to exactly 3 digits). Fix the function, then run the verify tool with cmd: node --input-type=module -e "const m=await import('./lib/parse-adrs.mjs');if(m.normalizeAdrId('7')!=='ADR-007')throw new Error('got '+m.normalizeAdrId('7'));console.log('PASS')"
tasks.verify: node --input-type=module -e "const m=await import('./lib/parse-adrs.mjs');if(m.normalizeAdrId('7')!=='ADR-007')throw new Error('got '+m.normalizeAdrId('7'));if(m.normalizeAdrId('12')!=='ADR-012')throw new Error('pad2');if(m.normalizeAdrId('1234')!=='ADR-1234')throw new Error('4digit');console.log('PASS')"
tasks.expected: normalizeAdrId pads to 3 digits again; the 4-digit branch is untouched; verify exits 0.

tasks.task: In lib/index-records.mjs the function uniqueEdges no longer removes duplicates: given two edges with the same relation/from/to it returns both, but it must return one. Fix it, then run the verify tool with cmd: node --input-type=module -e "const m=await import('./lib/index-records.mjs');const e={relation:'supersedes',from:'ADR-001',to:'ADR-002'};if(m.uniqueEdges([e,{...e}]).length!==1)throw new Error('not deduped');console.log('PASS')"
tasks.verify: node --input-type=module -e "const m=await import('./lib/index-records.mjs');const e={relation:'supersedes',from:'ADR-001',to:'ADR-002'};if(m.uniqueEdges([e,{...e}]).length!==1)throw new Error('not deduped');if(m.uniqueEdges([e,{relation:'r2',from:'a',to:'b'}]).length!==2)throw new Error('over-deduped');console.log('PASS')"
tasks.expected: uniqueEdges keys by edgeKey and keeps the first of each identity; distinct edges still survive; verify exits 0.

tasks.task: In _prices.mjs the function costAtTier divides input tokens by the wrong scale, so costs come out 10x too high. Prices in PRICING are per 1,000,000 tokens. Fix the input term, then run the verify tool with cmd: node --input-type=module -e "const m=await import('./_prices.mjs');const c=m.costAtTier({input:1e6,output:0,cache_write:0,cache_read:0},'sonnet');if(Math.abs(c-3)>1e-9)throw new Error('got '+c);console.log('PASS')"
tasks.verify: node --input-type=module -e "const m=await import('./_prices.mjs');const c=m.costAtTier({input:1e6,output:0,cache_write:0,cache_read:0},'sonnet');if(Math.abs(c-3)>1e-9)throw new Error('input '+c);const d=m.costAtTier({input:0,output:1e6,cache_write:0,cache_read:0},'sonnet');if(Math.abs(d-15)>1e-9)throw new Error('output '+d);console.log('PASS')"
tasks.expected: The input term divides by 1e6 like the other three terms; output pricing is unchanged; verify exits 0.

tasks.task: In stream-staleness.mjs the function isZombieSuspect wrongly reports a zombie when the probe says the stream is alive is false. It must return true ONLY when the silence has passed the threshold AND probeOutcome.alive === true. Fix it, then run the verify tool with cmd: node --input-type=module -e "const m=await import('./stream-staleness.mjs');if(m.isZombieSuspect(100,50,{alive:false})!==false)throw new Error('false positive');if(m.isZombieSuspect(100,50,{alive:true})!==true)throw new Error('missed');console.log('PASS')"
tasks.verify: node --input-type=module -e "const m=await import('./stream-staleness.mjs');if(m.isZombieSuspect(100,50,{alive:false})!==false)throw new Error('false positive');if(m.isZombieSuspect(100,50,{alive:true})!==true)throw new Error('missed');if(m.isZombieSuspect(10,50,{alive:true})!==false)throw new Error('below threshold');console.log('PASS')"
